root_cause.text: The RDMA/core DMAH allocation handler in `drivers/infiniband/core/uverbs_std_types_dmah.c` failed to validate the user-controlled `cpu_id` from `UVERBS_ATTR_ALLOC_DMAH_CPU_ID` before passing it to `cpumask_test_cpu()`, allowing out-of-range indexing of the cpumask bitmap.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (dmah->cpu_id >= nr_cpu_ids) { ret = -EINVAL; goto err; }` immediately before `cpumask_test_cpu(dmah->cpu_id, current->cpus_ptr)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states the value was “passed directly to cpumask_test_cpu() without first verifying that the value is within the valid CPU range,” causing an out-of-bounds read via `test_bit()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check for dmah->cpu_id so invalid CPU IDs are rejected with -EINVAL before cpumask permission testing.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added after the existing setup/error path to validate that dmah->cpu_id is less than nr_cpu_ids; if it is out of range, ret is set to -EINVAL and execution jumps to the err label before calling cpumask_test_cpu().
intent_record.how: This prevents the handler from using an invalid CPU index in cpumask_test_cpu(), causing out-of-range cpu_id values to fail early with -EINVAL instead of proceeding to permission checking or triggering invalid access behavior.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is fully visible in the provided function body. In `UVERBS_HANDLER(UVERBS_METHOD_DMAH_ALLOC)`, the user-controlled `cpu_id` is copied from `UVERBS_ATTR_ALLOC_DMAH_CPU_ID` via `uverbs_copy_from(&dmah->cpu_id, attrs, UVERBS_ATTR_ALLOC_DMAH_CPU_ID);` and then used directly in `cpumask_test_cpu(dmah->cpu_id, current->cpus_ptr)` with no prior bounds check against the valid CPU range. This matches the root cause exactly: failure to validate the user-supplied `cpu_id` before passing it to `cpumask_test_cpu()`, enabling out-of-range cpumask bitmap indexing. The code only checks whether the CPU is allowed in the current task's cpumask, not whether `dmah->cpu_id` itself is within range. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and no fix is shown in this commit.
